title: Controlled transforms in smooth marked blowup charts
statement:
Let $N\hookrightarrow Z$ be a smooth closed pair of finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes, $E$ a finite ordered simple normal crossings boundary transverse to $N$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and $J\subset\mathcal O_N$ a coherent ideal [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $c\ge1$ and let $C\subset N$ be a smooth closed subscheme such that $J_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^c$ for every $x\in C$. Assume $C$ has normal crossings with $E$: locally in etale coordinates on $Z$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], $N$ and $C$ are coordinate subspaces and each $E_i$ is a coordinate hyperplane transverse to $N$. Centers contained in some $E_i$ are allowed. Let $\sigma:Z'\to Z$ be the blowup of $C$, $N'$ the scheme-theoretic strict transform, and $F$ the exceptional divisor [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-nagata-strict-transform].
Write $\mathcal I_{C,N}$ for the ideal sheaf of $C$ in $N$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Then $J\subseteq\mathcal I_{C,N}^c$. The schemes $Z'$ and $N'$ are smooth and of finite type, and $N'\cong\operatorname{Bl}_C N$. The old strict-transform boundary together with $F$ is again simple normal crossings and transverse to $N'$. If $(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ generate the coordinate ideal of $C$ in $N$, the charts of $N'$ over a component not contained in $C$ have coordinates $e=u_i$, $u_j/e$ for $j\ne i$, and the unchanged coordinates. Any component of $N$ contained in $C$ disappears from $N'$; if $C$ contains a component of $Z$, that ambient component also disappears. Empty schemes are allowed. The controlled transform $J'=e^{-c}\sigma^*J$ is a regular coherent ideal. If $J$ is nonzero on every component of $N$, then $J'$ is nonzero on every component of $N'$. These formulas, the support identification $N\prime\cong\operatorname{Bl}_C N$ and the ordered boundary commute with smooth base change. For a monomial $J=\prod_{j\in T}(u_j)^{a_j}$ and center $C=\bigcap_{j\in A}V(u_j)$ with $A\subseteq T$ and $\sum_{j\in A}a_j\ge c$, the $i$-chart, $i\in A$, has new exceptional exponent $a_F=\sum_{j\in A}a_j-c$, the strict-transform exponents remain $a_j$ for $j\ne i$, and the strict transform of $V(u_i)$ is absent from that chart. Outside the center the marked pair is unchanged.

source.place: Stacks Tags 0804 (divisors, lemma-blowing-up-affine), 0FUE (more-morphisms, lemma-etale-local-structure), 0FUT (more-morphisms, lemma-blowup); coordinate calculation for a smooth flag and a normal crossings boundary, and Taylor expansion along the smooth center for the ideal-power assertion.

proof.text: Work locally on the given smooth schemes and their closed subschemes. Finite type over the field $\mathbf Q$ implies Noetherian, since a field is Noetherian. Smoothness implies that every local ring is a normal domain, so the finitely many irreducible components of each of $Z,N,C$ are disjoint open and closed integral schemes. These assertions apply without separatedness of the whole scheme. We may therefore treat a component on which the center is the whole scheme separately from components where its complement is dense. If $C$ contains a component $D$ of $N$, then at its generic point $\eta$ the local ring of $N$ is a field and $\mathfrak m_\eta=0$; the order hypothesis forces $J_\eta=0$. An ideal in a domain injects into its fraction field, so $J|_D=0$.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (morphisms, lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 0357 (properties, lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles); the field and ideal observations are elementary.

proof.text: Put $I=\mathcal I_{C,N}$. At $x\in C$, set $R=\mathcal O_{N,x}$ and $B=R/I_x=\mathcal O_{C,x}$, a domain by step 1. The smooth closed immersion $C\hookrightarrow N$ is locally generated by a regular sequence, which stays regular in $R$. Its associated graded pieces $I_x^d/I_x^{d+1}$ are free $B$-modules with basis the degree-$d$ monomials in that sequence. For $f\in J_x$, prove $f\in I_x^d$ successively for $d=0,\ldots,c$. If $d<c$ and $f\in I_x^d$, its degree-$d$ class becomes zero after localizing $B$ at its zero prime: the corresponding point $\eta$ is the generic point of the component of $C$ through $x$, and $I_\eta=\mathfrak m_{N,\eta}$, while $J_\eta\subseteq I_\eta^c\subseteq I_\eta^{d+1}$. A free module over the domain $B$ injects into its localization over $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ (apply injectivity to each coefficient). Thus the class was zero and $f\in I_x^{d+1}$. Outside $C$, $I=\mathcal O_N$, so the inclusion is automatic. This proves $J\subseteq I^c$ as ideal sheaves, including $I_x=0$.

source.place: Tag 00LN (algebra, lemma-regular-quasi-regular), degreewise freeness from 061P/061N; apply to the smooth regular immersion of Tag 067U. The finite induction supplies the ideal-power assertion.

proof.text: Apply the ambient-closed strict-transform theorem to $N\hookrightarrow Z$ and center $C$. Its pulled-back center on $N$ is exactly $C$, hence canonically $N'\cong\operatorname{Bl}_C N$ with the specified map to $Z'$. The blowup is an isomorphism over $Z\setminus C$, and this identifies $N'\setminus F$ with $N\setminus C$. On a component contained in $C$, the center ideal is zero. The only affine chart of the zero ideal is the zero algebra $A[0/0]\subset A_0=0$, whose spectrum is empty; equivalently its Rees algebra has no positive degrees. Thus that component disappears, on $N$ and also on $Z$. If $C=\varnothing$, the complement is the whole scheme and both blowups are identities. These are scheme-theoretic conclusions, not merely equalities of underlying sets.

source.place: Tags 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine), 080E (lemma-strict-transform); zero-ideal charts and the complement assertion (02OS).

proof.text: Use the simultaneous etale coordinates assumed in the statement: write $N=V(z_1,\ldots,z_s)$ and $C=V(z_1,\ldots,z_s,u_1,\ldots,u_r)$, with remaining coordinates $w$. On a component meeting but not contained in $C$, $r+s>0$. In the polynomial model the listed center coordinates, in any order, are a regular sequence. The affine chart presentation for a regular sequence and the finite chart cover give, for each center coordinate $v$, the equations $a=v(a/v)$ for the other center coordinates $a$. Eliminating those $a$ leaves the polynomial coordinates $v$, all $a/v$, and $w$. On this chart the center ideal is $(v)$ and $v$ is a nonzerodivisor. The comparison for flat base change carries these charts to the actual etale coordinate neighbourhoods; base change of the coordinate map is etale. Thus the calculation is valid on an etale cover of the actual blowup, rather than assuming an etale ring is itself a polynomial ring.

source.place: Tag 0804; Tag 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up); the presentation uses Tag 0BIQ (more-algebra, lemma-blowup-regular-sequence). Compare more-morphisms, remark-relative-blowup preceding 0FUT.

proof.text: In a $u_i$-chart put $e=u_i$. The strict transform of $N$ is $V(z_1/e,\ldots,z_s/e)$: away from $e=0$ this is $N$, and its chart ring is etale over the polynomial ring in $e$, $u_j/e$ ($j\ne i$), and $w$; multiplication by $e$ is injective, so its closure adds no equations. A $z_i$-chart has no strict transform of $N$, since there $z_i/e=1$ whereas the strict-transform equations require all normal ratios to be zero. Equivalently use the canonical $\operatorname{Bl}_C N$ of step 3, whose cover consists precisely of the $u_i$-charts. Polynomial charts are smooth over $\mathbf Q$; etale maps are smooth, compositions are smooth, and smoothness descends from a surjective etale cover. The same argument for the ambient charts proves $Z'$ smooth, and the empty-source case is vacuous. Both blowups are proper over their respective original schemes, since their center ideals are finite type on Noetherian schemes. Proper implies finite type; composition with the given finite-type structure maps proves that $Z'$ and $N'$ are of finite type over $\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Tag 0FUT (more-morphisms, lemma-blowup) and remark-relative-blowup; Tag 02NS (divisors, lemma-blowing-up-projective); explicit strict-support calculation.

proof.text: Each old boundary equation is one of the $u$ or $w$ coordinates, never a $z$ coordinate, because the boundary is transverse to $N$. On a chart with denominator $v$, the strict transform of $V(v)$ is absent: its complement of $C$ has empty inverse image in this chart. For another center coordinate $a$, the strict transform of $V(a)$ is $V(a/v)$; for a boundary coordinate $w_k$ outside the center ideal it is $V(w_k)$. Indeed $a=v(a/v)$ and saturation by $v$ removes precisely the displayed factor $v$, since the resulting polynomial coordinate quotient has no $v$-torsion; this remains true on the etale chart. Add $F=V(v)$. These are distinct independent coordinate hyperplanes, so every intersection is empty or smooth of the expected codimension. The regular-intersection criterion descends along the etale cover. In every chart meeting $N'$, the equations of $N'$ are the $z_l/e$, independent of all these boundary equations. This proves the boundary remains simple normal crossings and transverse to $N'$, even when the center is contained in old boundary components. Retain the old labels in their order, omit empty transforms, and append the exceptional boundary; disjoint exceptional components may be given the common new label.

source.place: Tags 0804 and 0805; explicit coordinate/saturation calculation. The regular-intersection criterion is ILO VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), as recorded in def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary.

proof.text: On any actual affine blowup chart $A[I/a]$ of $N$, write $e=a$ (so $e=u_i$ on an adapted chart). Then step 2 and $I\mathcal O_{N'}=(e)$ imply that each pulled-back generator $f_l$ of $J$ is uniquely $e^c g_l$ with $g_l$ regular: expand $f_l$ as a finite sum of degree-$c$ products of generators of $I$ and use $b=e(b/e)$ for every center generator $b$. Uniqueness follows from injectivity of multiplication by $e$. Define $J'$ on this chart by the ideal $(g_l)$; it is independent of the generating list because the operation of dividing any relation by the nonzerodivisor $e^c$ preserves that relation. On overlaps, if $e'=h e$ for a unit $h$, then $g'_l=h^{-c}g_l$, so the generated ideals agree. Thus these local ideals glue to the intrinsic ideal $\mathcal I_{F|N'}^{-c}\,(J\mathcal O_{N'})\subset\mathcal O_{N'}$. They are quasi-coherent and finite type: on an affine chart they are the tilde ideal of the finite list $g_l$, and on a principal subopen they localize to that same list. As $N'$ is locally Noetherian (step 5), the coherent-if-and-only-if-quasi-coherent-finite-type theorem proves coherence. Here regular means that the generators have no poles, not that $J'$ is principal or a unit ideal.

source.place: Tags 0804, 02OS (exceptional effective Cartier divisor); coherence is Tag 01XZ (coherent, lemma-coherent-Noetherian). Division and the overlap formula are supplied explicitly.

proof.text: For the nonvanishing assertion, restrict to an integral component $D$ of $N$ not contained in $C$. Every nonempty chart of $\operatorname{Bl}_{C\cap D}D$ is a subring of the localization of an affine domain of $D$ at its denominator, hence is a domain and meets the inverse image of $D\setminus C$ densely. The chart overlaps on that dense open, so the blowup of $D$ is integral and has the same generic point and function field as $D$. There are no extra components supported only over $C$. At that generic point $e$ is invertible and the division gives $J'_\eta=J_\eta$. The hypothesis that $J$ is nonzero on $D$ implies $J_\eta\ne0$ by injectivity into the fraction field. Hence $J'$ is nonzero on every surviving component. Deleted components contribute no condition; in fact step 1 shows that the additional nonzero hypothesis precludes their occurrence.

source.place: Tag 0804; affine blowup algebras as subalgebras of localizations, and the complement isomorphism of 02OS.

proof.text:
For the monomial assertion substitute $u_i=e$ and $u_j=e v_j$ for $j\in A\setminus\{i\}$, leaving $u_j$ unchanged for $j\notin A$. Then the single monomial generator pulls back to
$$e^{\sum_{j\in A}a_j}\prod_{j\in A\setminus\{i\}}v_j^{a_j}\prod_{j\in T\setminus A}u_j^{a_j}.$$
Dividing by $e^c$ gives the exceptional exponent $\sum_{j\in A}a_j-c\ge0$ and exactly the stated unchanged strict-transform exponents. The $i$th old divisor is absent on this chart by step 6, so its exponent is not attached to a fictitious strict transform. This also covers zero exponents and equality $\sum_{j\in A}a_j=c$. If $A=\varnothing$, there is no $i$-chart (and the required inequality cannot hold for $c\ge1$).

source.place: Elementary substitution in the affine chart of Tag 0804.

proof.text: Let $g:\widetilde Z\to Z$ be smooth and pull back $N,C,J$. Smoothness gives flatness. Apply blowup flat base change once to $Z$ and once to $N$: the canonical comparisons identify the ambient blowups and $\operatorname{Bl}_{\widetilde C}\widetilde N$ with their pullbacks. The ambient-closed theorem then identifies the latter with the strict transform of $\widetilde N$, giving the claimed support identification after base change without a generic-point assumption. On affine charts the comparison takes each fraction $u_j/e$ to $g^*u_j/g^*e$. Flat tensor preserves the injection given by multiplication by $e$, so $g^*e$ remains a nonzerodivisor. Pulling back $e^cg_l=f_l$ therefore gives the unique identity $(g^*e)^c(g^*g_l)=g^*f_l$. Thus the controlled-transform ideal, including its overlap units, is exactly the pulled-back ideal, not merely an ideal with the same vanishing set. The monomial exponent formula is unchanged under this substitution. For the affine comparison in marked_blowup_chart_smooth_baseChange, multiplication by a is injective on R[I/a], since this chart is a subalgebra of R[1/a]. Tensor this injective linear map with the flat R-algebra S. Thus the exceptional-power torsion vanishes on S tensor_R R[I/a]. The existing kernel and surjectivity results for strictChartMap prove bijectivity. The image of I in R[I/a] is (a), directly from x=a(x/a), so the image K of J is contained in (a^c). Elementary ideal division gives K=(a^c)(K:a^c). Map this equality to the new chart, whose exceptional equation is again a nonzerodivisor; cancel that equation to identify the colon ideals. The existing pure-tensor formula gives the asserted ratio identity. This proves this affine theorem without any new unproved intermediate statement; the other three declarations retain the rest of the planned argument.

source.place: Tag 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up) and 080E; flat tensor preserves injections, followed by the displayed division identity.

proof.text: For each old divisor $E_j$, apply the same ambient-closed theorem to $E_j\hookrightarrow Z$: its strict transform is the blowup in the extended center ideal, also when $C$ is not contained in $E_j$. Flat base change for this blowup identifies its pullback with the new strict transform of the pulled-back $E_j$. The exceptional divisor is the inverse image of $C$, whose equation on each chart is $e$, so it too pulls back with its equation. All these identifications preserve their original labels; omitted empty divisors pull back to empty divisors and any further empty pullbacks are omitted. Smooth morphisms locally factor as etale morphisms to relative affine space, so their extra coordinates simply join the unchanged coordinates $w$; the independent-hyperplane calculation of step 6 still applies. Finally over the complement of $C$ the blowup is an isomorphism and the exceptional ideal is the unit ideal. The controlled transform, marking $c$, smooth support and ordered old boundary there are therefore precisely the original marked pair.
